sections.title: Interview bank U09: Parallelism, clusters, scheduling

keyTerms.definition: Original practice, role-derived material. Not actual lab questions.
A set of breadth, ladder, analytical, debug, scenario, and critique questions per unit.

recall.question: What is the provenance of this interview bank?
recall.answer: Original practice, role-derived. The questions are not actual lab questions.

keyTerms.definition: 2*(n-1)/n * S/BW: reduce-scatter then all-gather.
(p-1)/(m+p-1): idle stage time.
1: optimizer states. 2: +gradients. 3: +parameters.
(max - median)/median on the synchronous step.

recall.question: Write the ring all-reduce formula. Name the two passes.
Write the cluster MTBF formula.
recall.answer: Cluster MTBF = per-GPU MTBF / GPU count.

keyTerms.definition: 0.35 s per sync on the toy: bytes flat in n, latency not.
Ring for big S (bandwidth-optimal); tree for small S (latency-optimal).
All GPUs blasting one peer: the no-congestion assumption breaks.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 prices the data-parallel tax: S=20 GB, n=8, BW=100 GB/s. What is the ring all-reduce time and its scaling?
recall.answer: 2*7/8 * 20/100 = 0.35 s. Bytes: 2(n-1)/n -> 2 as n grows (nearly flat). Latency: 2(n-1) hops grow with n.

keyTerms.definition: Total steps: fill p-1, useful m, drain p-1.
Same bubble with less activation memory.
Uneven stages (e.g. embeddings at 2x) break the formula.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 computes the pipeline bubble at p=4, m=8. What is it, and where does the formula come from?
recall.answer: 3/11 = 27.3%. Fill takes p-1 steps, drain p-1: total m+p-1, useful m.

keyTerms.definition: Keep TP groups inside the node.
12x slower across the thin link on the toy.
4096 GPUs: 6.4 h MTBF, ~112 failures per 30 days.

recall.question: All-reduce 20 GB at n=8: intra-node 600 GB/s vs split 50 GB/s. A TP-8 job is split across the nodes: verdict?
recall.answer: Intra-node 0.058 s, split 0.70 s: 12x. Each TP sync costs 0.70 s: the job is dead. Move TP inside the node.

recall.question: Per-GPU MTBF 3 years: 256 vs 4096 GPUs. What does the 4096 number imply for checkpoint design?
recall.answer: 256 GPUs: 4.28 days MTBF, ~7 failures per 30 days. 4096: 6.4 h, ~112 failures. Checkpoint/restart must be fast, frequent, automatic: it dominates system design.

keyTerms.definition: The bug: forgot to divide by n (shards, not copies).
Per-GPU bytes fall as 1/n under ZeRO-3.

recall.question: D1. The sharding helper is meant to be ZeRO-3 but a 10B run still OOMs on 40 GB GPUs. What is the bug, the fix, and the invariant?
recall.answer: Bug: forgot to divide by n (shards, not copies). Fix: per_gpu = 16 * P / n. Invariant: per-GPU bytes fall as 1/n under ZeRO-3.

keyTerms.definition: Collective tax vanishes; bubbles, stragglers, memory caps remain.
Checkpointing becomes optional; spot always wins.
Best split with no comm tax, plus PP for memory.

recall.question: Interconnect bandwidth is infinite and free. Which parallelism taxes vanish, which remain, and what is the best split?
recall.answer: The collective tax vanishes (TP all-reduce, DP sync, MoE dispatch). Bubbles, stragglers, memory caps remain. Best split: TP everywhere plus PP for memory.

recall.question: GPUs never fail and preemption is impossible. What changes?
recall.answer: Checkpointing becomes optional (final save only). Scheduling drops preemption handling. Spot vs on-demand: spot always wins (discount with zero rework).

keyTerms.definition: MFU definition? Counting recompute as useful FLOPs invalidates.
A 10-minute burst is not a run.

recall.question: A paper claims “our scheduler achieves 95% MFU on 4096 GPUs.” What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) MFU definition? (2) Sustained? (3) All ranks? (4) Matched baseline? (5) Failures in the window?
